views.label: Brambleglass initial interaction
views.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Complete 16:9 whole-screen gameplay target on the 480x270 native grid, derived from the accepted live screenshot. Re-art the fixed workshop, two-gate divider, garden, courier, cauldron, WARM and FIZZ ingredients, Mira, dormant follow-up plots, top status ribbon, and bottom instruction ribbon as a warm late-afternoon Brambleglass Courier Yard. Preserve direct movement, E interaction, navigable floor, route-gate causality, actor scale, object anchors, and the ink/slate/mulberry/parchment/copper/cyan/coral/leaf/violet palette. Use crisp authored 16-bit pixel clusters, quiet readable status typography, short pixel world labels, and no runtime plate, dashboard, menu, extra character, hidden gate, decorative frame, generic purple card, mixed pixel density, watermark, or concept-art perspective.

views.label: Interaction — choose and brew
views.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Complete whole-screen gameplay target for Direction B, Inkcap Night Conservatory, derived from the accepted initial live-engine capture. Preserve the 480x270 shipping camera; the broad workshop, narrow divider with exactly two COOL and VENT openings, compact garden, courier, ingredient, cauldron, Mira, and dormant follow-up anchors; direct WASD movement and E interaction; and open navigable space. Re-art the world as moonlit indigo flagstone beneath glass rafters, brass alembics, inkcap mushrooms, mulberry soil, phosphor moss, cyan crystalline COOL gate, and saffron copper VENT gate. Use a compact dark ledger status band, a single bottom control sentence, calm readable status typography, pixel display type only for short world labels, crisp 1-2 native-pixel outlines, and one consistent authored pixel density. Initial state: no bottle, inactive gates, waiting Mira, dormant unlabeled prediction plots. Avoid moved topology, extra actors, generic cards, rounded panels, inventory UI, excessive borders, illegible copy, painterly or isometric treatment, hidden gates, watermark, or runtime-plate framing.

views.label: Action — post-brew carrying
views.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the selected Inkcap Night Conservatory world, fixed camera, palette, pixel density, environment, gates, Mira, anchors, and interface regions unchanged. Create the coherent post-brew action state: the sole courier stands at the cauldron, carries a separate cyan-and-coral corked bottle, the cauldron shows a compact magenta/cyan bubble crest and brass rim response, ingredient pedestals settle, both route gates remain inactive and equally plausible, Mira waits, and prediction plots stay dormant. Status communicates FIZZ FORWARD and W2 F3 UNROUTED; the bottom instruction communicates carry through exactly one COOL or VENT gate. No new panel, path, actor, object, border, overlap, watermark, or unrelated effect.

views.label: Feedback — vent changed bottle
views.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit plus duplicate-courier correction. Keep the selected world, camera, geometry, palette, props, UI regions, and one consistent pixel density unchanged. Show exactly one courier just right of the VENT gate carrying a leaf-green balanced bottle; open only the lower copper VENT louvers; emit a compact saffron puff and one fading fizz spark; keep COOL inactive, Mira waiting and facing the courier, and follow-up plots dormant. Status communicates W2 F2 VENTED and bottom feedback communicates that VENT released fizz and delivery should continue to Mira. Remove any duplicate courier by restoring continuous workshop flagstone. No extra actors, moved anchors, new controls, panel, border, watermark, or unrelated motion.

views.label: Resolution — balanced relief and prediction
views.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the selected world, camera, geometry, palette, anchors, pixel density, and interface family. Show immediate successful delivery: exactly one empty-handed courier beside Mira, Mira makes a small relieved bounce with a leaf-green smile cue and balanced cyan/coral motes, cauldron and gates are idle, and the two dormant garden plots activate independently at their existing anchors as WARM+COOL and FIZZ+VENT without becoming cards. Status communicates BALANCED RELIEF and no bottle; bottom feedback asks for the next-batch prediction. Keep choices separated from characters and UI. No new actors, paths, panels, outer border, overlap, watermark, or unrelated effect.

views.label: Transition — next plan committed
views.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit plus position correction. Starting from the selected resolution screen, move the sole courier from Mira to immediately above the left garden prediction plot, keep WARM and FIZZ ingredient pedestals in the workshop, select WARM+COOL with a crisp leaf-green double ring and one upward mote, disable FIZZ+VENT with dark soil and a low-saturation saffron outline, keep Mira calm, and keep all other world and UI geometry unchanged. Status communicates BALANCED RELIEF and NEXT WARM+COOL; bottom feedback communicates that the result informed another choice. Exactly one courier, both choices inside the garden, no moved topology, new panel, actor, border, overlap, watermark, or unrelated motion.

continuityRules: Courier and Mira identity, native footprint, pivot, and world anchor remain stable through every beat.
Ambient loops are offset, low-amplitude, and subordinate to current interaction and consequence motion.
Effects originate at the real cauldron, gate, bottle, recipient, or plot state change and disappear without hiding authoritative state.
No animation moves collision boundaries, closes a traversable gate, obscures an action cue, or displaces an interactive anchor.
Interruption leaves the current potion, route, delivery, and follow-up state visibly correct.

findings.hypothesis: A restrained moonlit conservatory can add authored identity and controlled life without changing the accepted embodied loop when live geometry remains authoritative and generated screens remain reference-only.

experienceContract.typography: Hybrid: short pixel display labels and measured code-native humanist status, quantity, feedback, and recovery text.
controlledLife: delivery anticipation and attributable Mira reaction

componentMap.decomposition: Environment layers, actors, interactive props, carried potion, effects, and UI remain independent engine consumers with explicit bounds, anchors, states, layers, animation needs, prompts, and target-hash lineage.

opportunities.issue: Capture the one-line invalid-interaction recovery state during downstream integration; it is fully specified in the experience contract but does not have a dedicated raster reference.
evidence: design/scene-targets/scene-target.json defines recovery as a fixed bottom-ribbon replacement while preserving the complete world.

Both complete factory-owned traces use shipping input and record brewing at 3.5667s, route transformation at 5.6167s, delivery plus attributable reaction at 6.0167s, and next-plan commitment at 7.3667s; both scenarios passed with 38 distinct 1440x810 frames and no violations.
The 480x270 live geometry basis matches every center pixel of the first-session 1440x810 frame at time 0 under exact 3x normalization, tying the target contract to the accepted shipping-camera scene.
All six proposed target images exist at exactly 480x270 and match their declared SHA-256 pins.

Direction A and Direction B were reviewed as separate complete screens. Direction B wins because it preserves more open navigation, makes the two route gates one legible hinge, keeps Mira as the destination focus, and leaves follow-up plots visibly dormant before delivery.

Across the five selected states, the sole courier, cauldron, route gates, Mira, bottle state, prediction plots, status band, and context band remain coherent without modal takeover or accidental peer-region overlap.
All 19 component crops remain in viewport bounds and reference the approved hash. The only region intersections are the three explicitly declared playfield overlays.

metadata.hypothesis: A moonlit conservatory with a quiet code-native ledger and state-linked gate, bottle, recipient, and prediction motion can make the accepted loop feel inhabited while keeping direct navigation and causal attribution more legible than a warmer prop-dense courtyard.

surfaces.rule: One continuous structural surface; content changes without width reflow or new panels.
Appears only beside the reachable physical target and never competes with another E cue.
One concise message replaces the prior message; no stack, log, modal, or scrolling copy.
State belongs to a world prop; UI supplies only the anchored label and focus/selection cue.

ambientContinuity: One workshop lamp breathes across three low-amplitude values.
Two mushroom caps glint on different offsets, never simultaneously.
Mira blinks and shifts one shoulder while waiting.
Glasslight moves one value step without scrolling the floor or collision edges.
interactionResponse: Only the reachable ingredient, cauldron, Mira, or plot owns the active E cue.
Focus raises a prop or cue by one native pixel and settles within 120 ms.
Brew input links courier anticipation to cauldron response and bottle appearance.
gameplayConsequence: The VENT gate opens before the puff reaches the bottle and W2 F3 becomes W2 F2.
Mira turns before relief, reacts before result copy, and exposes choices only after the reaction reads.
Prediction selection animates the chosen world plot and visibly disables the alternative.
transitionMotion: Status content swaps in fixed bounds after the corresponding world response.
Follow-up plots transition dormant to active to selected/disabled without a camera cut.
All short effects settle to a persistent authoritative world or UI state.
reject: Frozen tableau with text-only state changes.
Unrelated particle loops or every-prop animation quotas.
Camera shake that obscures the route or actor anchor.
Ambient motion that resembles an interaction affordance.

antiPatterns: Generated whole-screen image loaded as the runtime world.
Environment plate containing courier, Mira, gates, bottle, prediction choices, labels, collisions, or feedback.
Generic purple cards, arbitrary rounded panels, nested decorative frames, or a dashboard around the playfield.
Tiny pixel font used for need, potion quantities, consequence, or recovery sentences.
Different pixel densities, non-integer runtime scaling, smoothed filtering, or resized unrelated motifs.
Route buttons, automatic travel, teleportation, proxy counters, or hidden gate choices.
Labels colliding with courier, Mira, prediction plots, gates, or the bottom context ribbon.
Effects or ambient loops not caused by current world state.
